format: 16-team Superflex Dynasty · NON-PPR (standard scoring) · no taxi squad · 2-round draft (32 picks)

classRead.summary: A WR-heavy class with a historically weak QB crop. Fernando Mendoza is the only QB worth a first-round rookie pick (top-3 in Superflex); Carson Beck and the rest are Round-3 values. Five WRs went in Round 1 of the NFL draft, eight in the first two rounds — the strength of this class is exactly where your picks are NOT, so the play at 15/16 is the second WR tier, a falling RB, or a trade.
classRead.qbNote: Do NOT reach for a rookie QB at 15/16 — it's a bad class. Solve Superflex QB via the vet market (Flacco went for a 2nd in this league last October).
classRead.noTaxiNote: No taxi squad: year-one usability matters. A redshirt project burns an active roster spot all season.
classRead.twoRoundNote: Only 32 picks exist — with 16 deep dynasty rosters the pool is picked clean, so we draft 2 rounds. That means anyone likely to slip past ~32 (ADP 33+) goes UNDRAFTED and is a FREE add after the draft. Never spend a pick on a player you can pick up Sunday morning for nothing.
classRead.scoringNote: NON-PPR changes the WR math: volume slot catchers lose their per-catch premium; yards-and-TD profiles and RBs gain. Weigh big-play ability over reception count.

myRosterRead.core: Bijan Robinson (2023 1.02) is the franchise. Cooper Kupp (acquired from the Machines, Aug 2024) is aging out — a young-WR succession piece is the biggest need.
myRosterRead.qb: QB room thin since the Dak trade (Nov 2024, to Porkys for two 1sts). Mac Jones came back in the Jonnu Smith deal. Superflex hole — but fix it with a vet trade, not this class.
myRosterRead.strategy: NON-PPR strategy, with names: 15: Nicholas Singleton if there (the Bijan running mate — must-have RB tier, Pollard expiring) OR the top Tier-2 WR faller (Boston). 16: the other of those, or trade 16 down into 17-23 for a future 2nd. Prefer TD/yardage WR profiles over slot-volume in this scoring. No QBs, no TEs, no reaching for players you can get free after pick 32.

pickCurveNote: TOP-3 PREMIUM: picks 1-3 are a closed shop in the SCFL — they trade only for another top pick or a future top-3 / equivalent, NEVER for a bundle of mid/late firsts. Note the cliff from 3 (820) to 4 (660). Picks 15-16 are solid late firsts, not top-3 currency; two of them together (~$66) do not approach a single top-3 pick (~$82-100).
tradeNotes: Only 32 picks exist. A late 2nd (28-32) is barely above waiver value — treat late 2nds as cheap sweeteners in trades, not real capital.
Moving up: cost is steep and unnecessary — your targets (Branch tier) live at 13-18, not 8-12. Only move up if a Tier-2 WR (Concepcion/Boston/Williams) slides past 10 and the Machines start circling.
Moving down from 16: good play ONLY into the 17-24 range (still real players). Past ~24 you are trading a real pick for near-waiver value — demand a future 1st/2nd instead of more 2026 late picks.
Keith rule: any faller you want, assume Keith at 17 wants him too — that is the real deadline on your 15/16 decisions.
The undrafted pool is your third pick: with ADP 33+ players going undrafted, plan two draft picks AND a waiver-sprint list for the minute the draft ends.

priceGuide: League market laws: players buy picks (most SCFL pick trades are player-for-pick). Current mid-1st ≈ future 1st. Up ~5 slots in the 20s ≈ a future 2nd. Early 2nd (17-22) ≈ a solid vet starter. Late 2nd (25-32) ≈ a depth vet or future 2nd. Top-10 ≈ a star player or a startable QB.

scoutingReports.name: Nicholas Singleton
scoutingReports.report: THE RB TARGET IN YOUR WINDOW. Penn State workhorse build; drafted by Tennessee where Tony Pollard is on an expiring contract after an inefficient year — clear path to the backfield as soon as 2026. Rated a MUST-HAVE dynasty rookie RB (consensus ~RB14 dynasty). Production plateaued late at PSU (Allen out-produced him in 2025) but the situation is the best of the mid-round RBs. Non-PPR loves him: early-down carries and goal-line work. If he is on the board at 15/16, he is the Bijan running mate the strategy calls for.

scoutingReports.name: Kaytron Allen
scoutingReports.report: Penn State s OTHER back — out-produced Singleton in 2025 but fell to the 6th round (draft-capital red flag). Landed in a muddy Washington room (Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White). Limited receiving juice — matters less in our non-PPR, but he profiles as RB4/5 with theoretical short-term RB2 upside if the room breaks right. Dynasty consensus: SOFT TARGET (~RB20). Fine late-2nd swing; do NOT spend 15/16.

scoutingReports.name: Demond Claiborne
scoutingReports.report: 5-9, 188, 4.37 speed out of Wake Forest (1,049 yds/11 TD junior year). 6th-rounder to Minnesota where both incumbent RBs are FAs after 2026 — sneaky path to the future RB1 job. Dynasty market: ~RB80, going rounds 3-4 of rookie drafts — which in OUR 2-round draft means he likely goes UNDRAFTED. Waiver-sprint list, not a pick.

scoutingReports.name: Zachariah Branch
scoutingReports.report: Ex-five-star, elite returner, 78% slot rate, 5.2 aDOT at USC. Landed in Tommy Rees quick-game offense — immediate touches. The catch: that is a PPR profile, and we are NON-PPR — short-catch volume without per-catch points shrinks his edge. Take at 15 only on talent conviction; otherwise the RB (Singleton) is the sounder standard-scoring pick.

scoutingReports.name: Denzel Boston
scoutingReports.report: 6-4 X-receiver, Washington. Big camp buzz (moved up boards all summer); contested-catch and red-zone profile — TD-dependent, which non-PPR REWARDS. Shares the Cleveland depth chart with fellow rookie Concepcion. Usually gone by ~15 — if he is there, he is the faller you take.

scoutingReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
scoutingReports.report: Indiana product, Jets Day-2 pick. Camp buzz in New York went to Adonai Mitchell instead — role uncertain year one. Talent is real (ball skills, bend); situation is the concern. Coin-flip at your picks; fine at 16, better if he slides to a trade-down slot.

scoutingReports.name: Antonio Williams
scoutingReports.report: Clemson slot, productive underneath. Immediate-snaps path in Washington with a young QB. Another catch-volume profile discounted by our non-PPR — real player, wrong scoring fit to reach for.

scoutingReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
scoutingReports.report: TE1 of the class (Oregon). Athletic seam threat. TEs take 2 years to pay off and we have no taxi squad — only worth 15/16 if you specifically need the position; usually gone ~10 anyway to a TE-needy room.

scoutingReports.name: Eli Stowers
scoutingReports.report: TE2 (Vanderbilt), converted QB, YAC athlete. Philly creative usage appeal. Same TE caveat: slow payoff + no taxi = not a 15/16 play.

scoutingReports.name: KC Concepcion
scoutingReports.report: NC State separator with YAC juice; the other Cleveland rookie. Floor+ceiling combo; usually top-8 gone. Chase only if he slides past 10 and the price is right.

scoutingReports.name: Jadarian Price
scoutingReports.report: Notre Dame, RB2 of the class, goes ~1.6. Explosive, fresh legs (split backfield with Love). Gone way before 15 — relevant only to a big trade-up, which the board says not to make.

scoutingReports.name: Caleb Douglas
scoutingReports.report: 6-4, 4.39 deep X for a Slowik offense that lacks one — yards-and-TD profile that FITS non-PPR perfectly. But ADP ~33: borderline last pick of our 2-round draft with a real chance he slides out. Right type, wrong price at 16 — a late 2nd gets him, or the waiver sprint does.

scoutingReports.name: Elijah Sarratt
scoutingReports.report: Talent bet buried behind Bateman and fellow rookie Jakobi Lane in a bottom-5 volume pass game. ADP ~35 — likely UNDRAFTED here. Post-draft add, never a pick.

scoutingReports.name: Skyler Bell
scoutingReports.report: UConn producer to a contender; round-2 rookie range. Depth-chart fight in Buffalo. Late-2nd or waiver.

scoutingReports.name: Brenen Thompson
scoutingReports.report: Pure vertical speed (1,054 yds at Mississippi State). Field-stretcher role for the Chargers; spike-week profile, thin floor. Late-2nd or waiver.

scoutingReports.name: Jalen Nailor
scoutingReports.report: VETERAN free agent in the pool, not a rookie — speed depth piece. That he shows on the draftable board at all tells you how thin the pool is; roster filler, never a pick.

scoutingReports.name: Jake Tonges
scoutingReports.report: VETERAN journeyman TE in the FA pool. Waiver-tier roster filler; ignore on draft day.
